title: Spot the fake request
summary: You never need your UPI PIN or an OTP to receive money; scammers rely on hurry and fake links.

variants.markdown:
**English draft for R5 review.**

On UPI you enter your PIN only when money is **leaving** your account. If someone says "enter your PIN to receive ₹2,000", it is a scam. Never share an OTP or PIN with anyone, even someone who says they are from the bank.

Scammers send fake links, collect requests and calls that sound urgent: "your account will be blocked today". Stop, don't click, and check with a trusted adult or the bank's official number. If money is lost, call the cybercrime helpline 1930 quickly. Gullak uses virtual play money only.

questions.prompt: A buyer says: "Enter your UPI PIN to receive ₹2,000 for your old cycle." What is true?

options.text: You never need a PIN to receive money, so this is a scam
It's normal; receiving money needs a PIN
It's fine if the amount is small

questions.explanation: A UPI PIN only approves money going out of your account.

questions.prompt: A message says your bank account will be blocked today unless you click a link. What is the red flag?

options.text: The pressure to act fast through a link

questions.explanation: Hurry plus a link is the most common phishing pattern.

questions.prompt: A caller "from the bank" asks Nani for the OTP she just got. What should she do?

options.text: Hang up and call the bank's official number herself
Share it quickly so the account isn't blocked

questions.explanation: Banks never ask for an OTP. Pause and check through an official channel.
